transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just feel worn out almost every day. It's like... even after a full night's sleep, my body and my head are still just dragging when I have to get up for my cashier shift.
Do you unintentionally doze off or fall asleep during the day?
No, I don't really doze off or fall asleep during the day. I mean, I'm tired and dragging, like I said, but I'm awake. I just have to kind of push through my shifts at the store.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days?
No, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or depressed. It's really just that I'm so worn out all the time, like I was saying. But my mood itself isn't really down.
Has anyone ever noticed that you stop breathing or gasp for air while you’re asleep?
No, nobody's ever mentioned anything like that to me. As far as I know, I breathe just fine when I'm sleeping.
Has anyone ever told you that you snore loudly while you sleep?
No, not that I know of. Nobody's ever complained about me snoring or anything like that. I'm pretty sure I sleep quiet.
Do you often wake up with a headache?
No, I don't think so. I mean, maybe once in a great while, but definitely not often. I usually wake up feeling okay in that regard, just tired.
How long have you been feeling this worn out?
It's been, um, about a year and three months now. That's when our older relative moved in with us, and I've just been feeling worn out ever since.
Since your relative moved in, have you been feeling unusually stressed or worried?

Yeah, I have. It just feels like my mind is always jumping from one thing to the next lately. I'm constantly thinking about money, or, you know, having our relative staying with us and how stressed my wife has been. And then I start worrying about my church duties, or wondering if I'm messing up at work. It's just a lot of things on my mind all at once.
When you start worrying, how difficult is it for you to stop or control the worrying?

It's pretty difficult, honestly. I try telling myself to just pray on it, or, you know, just leave it alone. But once a worry starts up in my head, it just keeps rolling right into another one. It's like I can't stop it until I'm sitting there thinking through every bad way the day could possibly go.
Do you often feel restless or unable to sit still because of your worry?

Not really, no. I mean, I can sit still just fine. It's not like I'm pacing around the house or anything like that. The worrying is mostly just... well, it's all up in my head, not really something that makes me feel like I need to move around.
When you’re worrying, do you find it difficult to concentrate on things like work or conversations?

Yeah, it definitely messes with my focus. Like, at work... I'm a cashier, and sometimes I'll be looking right at the register screen, but my mind is completely somewhere else. I'll be thinking about things at home or worrying about the bills. Because of that, I'll lose track of what I'm doing and end up having to recount the drawer, or I'll catch a small mistake I made just because I wasn't paying attention.
When you’re worrying, do you often feel physically tense, such as having tight or aching muscles?
No, I haven't really noticed that. My muscles don't get tight or sore from it. Like I said, it's mostly just my mind going a mile a minute. I don't really feel it in my body like that.
Do you often have trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

Yeah, sleep is definitely a problem. Most nights, I'll get into bed feeling really tired, but then... my brain just turns on. I just lie there going over all the bills, thinking about my work schedule for the week, worrying if everyone at home is doing okay. It takes me a long time to actually drift off. And even when I finally do get to sleep, I usually wake up the next morning feeling like I never really settled down or got any real rest.
Over the past six months, on how many days would you say you’ve had this excessive worry?

Well, it's been pretty much every day for a while now. I'd say it started about a year and three months ago. That's when my older relative moved in with us, and the worrying just kind of started then and hasn't really stopped. So, yeah, definitely most days over the last six months.
